title: M/S. Apana Motor Finance vs Venkatesh. K.V on 9 July, 2015
full_text: M/S. Apana Motor Finance vs Venkatesh. K.V on 9 July, 2015 IN THE COURT OF THE XXVII ADDL. CHIEF METROPOLITON MAGISTRATE, NRUPATHUNGA ROAD, BENGALURU CITY. Dated this the 9th day of July-2015 :: PRESENT :: SRI. MALLANAGOUDA, B.Com., LL.B., XXVII Addl. C.M.M., Bengaluru City. C.C. NO. 19831/2013 COMPLAINANT: M/s. Apana Motor Finance, 60, Kilari Road, Bangalore-560053, Rep. by its Manager, Mr. Manish Doshi, S/o Late. Jeevanchand Doshi, Aged about 32 years, (Rept. by Sri. H.C. Ramesh. Adv.) V/S ACCUSED: Venkatesh. K.V. S/o Venkataswamy, Aged about 36 years, 923, 4th Cross, 1st main, Vijayananda Nagar, Nandini Layout, Bangalore-560096. (Rept. by Sri. K. Utpal Kumar. Adv.) Judgment 2 C.C.19831/2013 OFFENCE COMPLAINED OF : U/Sec. 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act . PLEAD OF THE ACCUSED : Not guilty. FINAL ORDER : Accused is convicted DATE OF ORDER : 09-07-2015 (MALLANAGOUDA) XXVII Addl.CMM., Bengaluru. *** :: JUDGMENT : : This is the case in which the complainant has filed the complaint against the accused under Section.200 Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 2. The brief facts of the complainant's case are as under: The complainant is doing hire purchase business, accused has purchased vehicle bearing No. K.A.04 - C-3738 by borrowing Rs.1,30,000/- from complainant by entering into hire purchase agreement, as per terms of the said agreement accused shall pay 23 monthly installments of Judgment 3 C.C.19831/2013 Rs.7,500/- each and one installment of Rs.4,300/- which amounts to Rs.1,76,800/-, however accused has paid few installments and subsequently he has failed to pay the remaining monthly installments and became chronic defaulter. When the complainant has demanded for payment of dues on various occasions on 22-07-2013 accused has agreed to pay the entire amount and issued cheque bearing No.753018, dated: 22-07-2013 for Rs.1,25,000/- drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Sanjayanagar, Bangalore, but when complainant has presented the said cheque to bank for encashment the same has been dishonoured and returned with an endorsement as 'Funds Insufficient", after that complainant got issued legal notice dated: 26-07-2013 to accused, but the notice sent through RPAD is returned unserved as unclaimed, even after service of notice also accused has not paid the cheque amount. Thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Judgment 4 C.C.19831/2013 3. After service of summons, accused has appeared before this court and pleaded not guilty for the offence under Section.138 Negotiable Instruments Act. Hence, the trial has been conducted against him for the said offence. 4. On the basis of the above facts, following points have arisen for my consideration: POINTS 1. Whether complainant proves beyond reasonable doubt that the accused borrowed Rs.1,30,000/- from the complainant and to repay the said amount accused issued cheque bearing No. 753018, dated: 22-07-2013 for Rs.1,25,000/- drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Sanjayanagar, Bangalore, but when complainant has presented the said cheque to Bank for encashment, the same is dishonoured and returned with an endorsement as "Funds Insufficient", after that complainant got issued legal notice dated: 26-07- 2013 to accused, even after issuance of notice also accused has not paid cheque amount. Thereby the accused is liable for conviction for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act? 2. What order? 5. In support of its case, complainant examined one witness as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Exs.P1 to Judgment 5 C.C.19831/2013 P16 on its behalf. On the other hand accused has not produced any oral evidence but he got marked document at Ex.D1 on his behalf. 6. Heard arguments. 7. My findings on the above points are as under: Point No.1: In the affirmative Point No.2: As per final order, for the following: REASONS 8. POINT NO.1: It is the case of the complainant that by entering into hire purchase agreement with the complainant on 06-01-2012 accused has borrowed Rs.1,30,000/- for purchase of vehicle bearing No. K.A.04 C- 3738 agreeing to repay the borrowed amount in monthly installments, but subsequently he failed to pay the installments and when complainant demanded the accused on various occasions, finally on 22-07-2013 accused has agreed to pay the entire due and issued cheque bearing Judgment 6 C.C.19831/2013 No.753018, dated: 22-07-2013 for Rs.1,25,000/- drawn on Karnataka Bank Ltd., Sanjaynagar, Bangalore, on presentation the cheque has been dishonoured with endorsement 'Funds Insufficient', after that complainant got issued legal notice dated: 26-07-2013, even after service of notice also accused has not paid the cheque amount. Thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 9. During evidence P.W.1 namely Manish Doshi has filed his affidavit as chief-examination in which he once again restated the facts alleged in the complaint as discussed above. In cross-examination he denied suggestions regarding not having authority to file complaint and to give evidence for complainant, issuance of 10 blank cheques by the accused at the time of sanctioning the loan itself and filing present case by misusing one of such cheque. 10. The complainant got marked documents like Power of Attorney, Bank endorsement and Notice copy etc. Judgment 7 C.C.19831/2013 11. On the other hand accused got marked document at Ex.D1 which is the document issued by the complainant regarding re-possession of the vehicle. 12. During arguments learned counsel for complainant has argued that as the accused himself admitted that he had borrowed some money from the complainant and he has failed to produce the evidence regarding repayment of loan borrowed by him, admittedly cheque in question is belongs to accused and signature in the cheque is also belongs to accused, it is necessary to presume that the accused has issued the cheque in question for payment of legally dischargeable debt and burden lies on the accused to rebut the said presumption for which accused has not produced any evidence, therefore accused is liable for conviction. In support of his said arguments he has relied upon the following judgments: AIR 2014 S.C.630 A.C. Narayanan V/s. State of Maharashtra Judgment 8 C.C.19831/2013 With G. Kaamalakar V/s. M/s. Surana Securities Ltd., & Anr. A. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) Ss.138, 142 - Dishonour of cheque - Complaint - Filing of, through power of attorney is perfectly legal and competent. B. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881), Ss.138, 142, 145 - Criminal P.C. (2 of 1974), S.200 - Dishonour of cheque - Issuance of process - Power of attorney holder possessing due knowledge of transaction - Can depose and verify on complaint in order to prove its contents - Complainant is required to make specific assertion as to knowledge of power of attorney holder in impugned transaction. *** 2007 (3) Crimes 120 (SC) C.C. Alavi Haji V/s. Palapetty Muhammed & Anr. When notice is sent by registered post by correctly addressing drawer of cheque, mandatory requirement of issue of notice in terms of Clause (b) of proviso to section.138 stands complied with. Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 , Section.138(b) - Complaint alleging dishonour of cheque - Averment made in complaint p that even though complainant issued lawyers notice intimating dishonour of cheque and demanded payment same was returned saying that accused was out of station - No averment in complaint that notice was sent at correct address of drawer of cheque by registered post acknowledgment due - Returned envelope was however annexed to complaint and it, formed a part of complaint which showed that notice was sent by registered post Judgment 9 C.C.19831/2013 acknowledgment due to correct address and was returned with an endorsement that addressee was abroad - Held requirements of Section.138 were sufficiently complied with in fact of the case. *** AIR 2010 S.C.1898 Rangappa V/s. Mohan A. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) S.138 - Dishonour of cheque - On account of 'stop payment' instructions sent by accused to Bank in respect of post dated cheque - S.138 is attracted Insufficient of funds in account, irrespective. *** 2013 ACD 1131 (P&H) Anil Kumar Sharma V/s. State of Haryana and another Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) Ss.138, 139 - Dishonour of cheque - Conviction - Complainant had given loan of Rs.1,50,000/- to the accused - Cheque issued by accused for re-payment of loan amount was dishonoured - Accused did not deny his signature on cheque - Accused could not lead any evidence as contemplated under Section.139 as he did not chose to file reply to the notice - Findings of fact recorded by trail court to said effect - Appellate Court affirmed the findings of fact recorded by trial court - No interference. *** AIR 2001 S.C.2895 K.N. Beena Judgment 10 C.C.19831/2013 V/s. V. Muniyappan & another Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) Ss.138, 139, 118 - Cheque dishonour complaint - Burden of proving that cheque had not been issued for any debt or liability - Is on the accused - Denial averments in reply by accused are not sufficient to shift burden of proof on to the complainant - Accused has to prove in trial by leading cogent evidence that there was no debt or liability - Setting aside of conviction on basis of some formal evidence led by the accused - Not proper. *** 2013 ACD 59 (KER) Gopinatha Kurup V/s. State of Kerala Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) S.138 - Dishonour of cheque - Discharge of legal debt - Accused borrowed money from complainant and issued cheque to discharge debt which was dishonoured - Defence plea that accused had issued a blank signed cheque which was misused by complainant - No evidence was adduced by him to prove his case - As execution of cheque was admitted by accused, presumption as envisaged under Section.118 and 139 is available - Conviction of accused is proper. *** ILR 2001 KAR 4127 S.R. Muralidar V/s. Ashok. G.Y. Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - (Central Act No.26 of 1881)v - Section.138 - In a cheque Bounce case complainant has challenged the order of acquittal accepting Judgment 11 C.C.19831/2013 the defence of the drawer of the cheque that the complainant who is his business associate and was allowed to deal with the accounts and bank transactions has mis-used a cheque signed by him and the same is misutilized to fasten the false liability. High Court set aside the acquittal on the ground that there is no positive version of defence and the accused has not examined himself and from pleas taken up by picking out of context the statements made in the cross- examination and from the statement made in reply of the Accused, a hazy defence theory is sought to be built up. *** (2001) 7 S.C.C.417 Charanjit Singh Chadha & Ors V/s. Sudhir Mehra Contract - Hire purchase contract - Held, recovery of possession of goods by owner-financier as per terms of the hire-purchase agreement, does not amount to a criminal offence - Such as agreement is an executory contract of sale, conferring no right in rem on the hirer until the conditions for transfer of the property to him have been fulfilled - Held, on facts, where respondent hirer had defaulted in installment payments of motor vehicle and agreement specifically provided that appellant financiers were entitled to repossess the vehicle in case of default and their agents were authorized to enter any premises for the purpose, and appellants had actually recovered possession of the vehicle, no offence was made out against the appellants - High Court erred in dismissing their petition under S.482 Criminal Procedure Code challenging issue of summons on complaint filed under Ss.406/420/120-B and 379 Indian Penal Code - Criminal Procedure Code , 1973, S.482 - Words and Phrases - "Hire-purchase agreements", "Finance Charge", "Executory Contract" - Penal Code, 1860, Ss.406/420/120- B and 379 - Held, on facts, offences not made out against financiers in hire-purchase agreement - Hire Purchase Act , Judgment 12 C.C.19831/2013 1972 - Ss.8 and 20 (not yet in pure) - Passing of property and restriction on owner's right to recover possession of goods. *** 2010 CRI. L.J. 814 K. Mathivanan V/s. Suriyakumar Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) S.138 - Dishonour of cheque - Accused had taken loan of Rs.85,000/- from complainant - Accused himself in reply notice admitted that he issued blank cheques by way of security for prompt repayment of sum of Rs.85,000/- Accused pleaded discharge of loan of Rs.85,000/- - No evidence in form of receipt or endorsement was produced by him - Conviction of accused is proper - Sentence of two months' simple imprisonment would meet ends of justice. *** 2010 CRI.L.J. (NOC) 1185 (MAD) U. Vanjinayagi V/s. Nagaraj Evidence Act (1 of 1872) S.45 - Comparison of signature on cheque - Permissibility - Case of dishonour of cheque - Accused had admitted signature available in cheque however raised doubt with regard to colour of ink found in cheque was different - Accused seeking comparison of Signature found in cheque with her admitted signature found in cheque with her admitted signature by sending same to forensic expert's opinion - Held, there is no specific bar under Negotiable Instruments Act for a cheque to be filled up by any person other than the drawer, the payee or holder in due course who might have authority to fill up blank cheque and the said instrument is legally valid - Rejection of Judgment 13 C.C.19831/2013 application for comparison proper - Moreso, when such plead was raised by accused after closure of evidence by prosecution. *** (2009)1 S.C.C.492 P. Venugopal V/s. Madan P.Sarathi A. Negotiable Instruments Act,1881 - Ss.139, 118(a) and 138 - Dishonour of cheque - Presumption in case of - Held, presumptions must be confined to mattes specified in Ss.139 and 118(a) - Other facts have to be proved by the party alleging them - Existence of debt or other liability - Held, has to be proved in the first instance by the complainant - Complainant said to have given hand loan and appellant in return issuing two cheques in complainant's favour - Courts below holding as a fact that granting of loan was proved by complainant - Burden of proving to the contrary shifted to appellant - Courts below further holding that appellant not able to discharge his burden - Held, no case made out for interference by the Supreme Court. *** 2001 AIR - Kant. H.C.R.2154 M/s. Devi Tyres V/s. Nawab Jan A. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) S.138 - Dishonour of cheque - Complaint - Criminal Court cannot embark upon any enquiry that goes behind act of issuance of cheque - If cheque was alleged to be issued for some special reasons and it was not intended to be enacted or honoured - Onus of establishing the same shifts squarely to accused. *** Judgment 14 C.C.19831/2013 13. On the other hand counsel for accused has filed written arguments, in which he questioned about authority of the person who represented complainant, issuance of cheque for payment of the amount and service of notice. In support of his said arguments he has relied upon the following judgments: 2008 CRI. L.J. 1509 Roy Joseph Creado & Ors V/s. Sk. Tamisuddin & Ors A. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) S.142 - Criminal P.C. (2 of 1974) Ss. 2(d), 200 - Dishonour of cheque - Complaint alleging - Must be signed and verified by complainant - Complainant signed and verified by special power of attorney holder of complainant - Can not be regarded as complaint within meaning of Negotiable Instruments Act - It would be incomplete complaint - Said defect could not be cured by signing and verifying complaint by complainant due to death of complainant meanwhile - Special Power of Attorney holder not being payee of cheque or holder thereof in due course complaint filed by him liable to be dismissed. *** 2004 (2) DCR 641 Ramesh V/s. Ganeshchandra & Ors Judgment 15 C.C.19831/2013 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - S.138 - Criminal Procedure Code , 1973 - Section.200, 202 and 482 - Dishonour of cheque - Power of attorney - Complaint by - Complaint can be presented by holder of power of attorney - But for purpose of further prosecution - Presence of complainant is essential - If complaint appears and gives his statement before court - Then there is no defect in filing complaint - Same shall be treated as cured - Petition dismissed. *** AIR 2014 S.C.630 A.C. Narayanan V/s. State of Maharashtra With G. Kaamalakar V/s. M/s. Surana Securities Ltd., & Anr. B. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881), Ss.138, 142, 145 - Criminal P.C. (2 of 1974), S.200 - Dishonour of cheque - Issuance of process - Power of attorney holder possessing due knowledge of transaction - Can depose and verify on complaint in order to prove its contents - Complainant is required to make specific assertion as to knowledge of power of attorney holder in impugned transaction. *** 2008(6) KAR. L.J.538 (S.C) Krishna Janardhan Bhat V/s. Dattatraya G. Hegde A. Negotiable Instruments Act,1881, Section.139 - Holder of cheque - Statutory presumption to be drawn in favour of - Only presumption is that he received cheque for discharge, in whole or in part of any debt or other liability - Though it pre-supposes legally enforceable debt, existence of Judgment 16 C.C.19831/2013 such debt is not a matter of presumption under Section.139 of the Act - Same has to be proved. *** 1995 CRI. L.J. 560 Shri. Taher N. Khambati V/s. M/s. Vinayaka Enterprises, Secunderabad & Ors. *** AIR 2008 (NOC) 1300 (MAD) S. Gopal V/s. D. Balachandran A. Negotiable Instruments Act (26 of 1881) Ss.20, 138 - Evidence Act (1 of 1872) - Blank cheque signed by drawer - Holder in due course has no authority to complete blank cheque delivered to him by drawer - S.20 applies only to blank pronote and bill of exchange and not to blank cheques- However, if drawer of cheque gives authority to payee or holder in due course to fill up cheque signed by him - Such a cheque is valid. *** 2004 (1) Crimes 567 Avon Organics Ltd. V/s. Poineer Products Limited & Ors. Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - Sections.5, 6, 87, 138 and 139 - Dishonour of cheque - Acquittal by trail court - Appeal - Respondent issued blank cheque without mentioning date and amount and sent it with a letter requesting complainant to present it after a month - Question whether blank cheque will come within definition of cheque? - If cheque is not drawn for a specified amount it Judgment 17 C.C.19831/2013 would not fall within definition of bill of exchange - Act of complainant in filling up amount portion and date was a material change and it could not be enforced even though it was issued for legal liability - Alteration without consent of party who issued the cheque rendered cheque invalid - Acquittal called for no interference. *** 2011 (5) KCCR 4223 M.B. Rajasekhar V/s. Savithramma Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - Section.138 - Dishonour of cheque - Offence of - Acquittal - Contents of cheque were in different handwriting - Perusal of signature of accused on cheque did not reveal that she had filled it in her own hand - Inference can be drawn that either cheque was blank or some other persons had filled its contents - Date on cheque found to be altered so as to validate it without any authentication - Accused pleading that she had issued a post dated cheque as security - Also raising probable defence - It is sufficient to rebut presumption - Acquittal not liable to be interfered with. *** 14. On perusal of the evidence of both the parties and arguments of their counsels it appears that regarding authority of Power of Attorney holder to present the complaint and represent the complainant is concerned as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in judgment reported in AIR-2014 S.C.630, even P.A. Holder can present Judgment 18 C.C.19831/2013 the complaint and give evidence on behalf of the complainant, therefore contention of the accused that the person who represented the complainant had no authority to do so is incorrect. 15. Regarding issuance of cheque for payment of legally dischargeable debt is concerned as admitted by the accused, accused has borrowed some money from the complainant for purchase of vehicle, he has not repaid the entire loan amount, therefore it clearly appears that as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court in different judgments relied by the complainant counsel as per Section.139 of Negotiable Instruments Act, presumption has to be drawn and burden lies on the accused to rebut the presumption, but accused has not at all entered into witness box and produced evidence to rebut the presumption. Even if accused is entitled to rebut the presumption by bringing on record some evidence from the witnesses examined by the complainant, by looking to evidence of P.W.1 it appears that Judgment 19 C.C.19831/2013 there is nothing brought on record by the accused to show that as on the date of cheque accused was not liable to pay anything to complainant, therefore as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in above referred judgement in AIR-2010 S.C.1898, even if cheque has been issued in blank, holder of the cheque is entitled to complete the cheque and if he proves existence of legally dischargeable debt, definitely accused is liable for punishment for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. 16. Regarding contention of the accused about non-service of notice is concerned as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in judgment reported in 2007(3) Crimes 120 (S.C.) when complainant has complied with the requirements of Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act and even after appearance before the court accused has not paid the cheque amount, therefore accused is not entitled to escape from his liability on the ground of non-service of notice. Therefore as discussed above when there is evidence to show that as on Judgment 20 C.C.19831/2013 the date of cheque accused was liable to pay some money to complainant, cheque in question is belongs to accused, signature in the cheque is also belongs to accused, on presentation cheque is dishonoured for the reason 'Funds Insufficient' and even after issuance of notice accused has failed to pay the cheque amount, thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Hence, the accused is liable for conviction for the said offence. Therefore, I answered Point No.1 in the affirmative. 17. POINT NO.2: In view of my findings on Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER Acting under Section.265 of Cr.P.C., accused is convicted for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Accused shall pay fine of Rs.2,50,000/-. Out of the fine amount Rs.2,40,000/- is ordered Judgment 21 C.C.19831/2013 to be paid to the complainant as compensation and remaining amount of Rs.10,000/- is ordered to be remitted to the State. Office is directed to issue free copy of the Judgment to the accused immediately. (Dictated to Stenographer, transcribed and computerized by him, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 9th day of July-2015.) (MALLANA GOUDA) XXVII Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru. ANNEXURE List of Witnesses examined on behalf of Complainant: PW.1 : Manish Doshi List of Exhibits marked on behalf of Complainant: Ex.P1 : Power of attorney Ex.P2 : Cheque Ex.P3 : Return Memo Ex.P4 : Notice Ex.P5 : Postal receipt Ex.P6 : Undelivered postal cover Ex.P7 : Agreement Ex.P8 : Voucher Ex.P9 : Consideration Letter Ex.P10 : On demand promissory note Ex.P11 : Letter Ex.P12 & 13 : Copy of letter Ex.P14 : Ledger Account Judgment 22 C.C.19831/2013 Ex.P15 : Certificate Ex.P16 : Certificate of registration List of Witnesses examined on behalf of the defence: None List of Exhibits marked on behalf of defence: Ex.D1 : Letter (MALLANA GOUDA) XXVII Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru. Judgment 23 C.C.19831/2013 Judgment pronounced in the open court. Operative portion of the judgment. ORDER Acting under Section.265 of Cr.P.C., accused is convicted for the offence punishable under Section.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act. Accused shall pay fine of Rs.2,50,000/-. Out of the fine amount Rs.2,40,000/- is ordered to be paid to the complainant as compensation and remaining amount of Rs.10,000/- is ordered to be remitted to the State. Office is directed to issue free copy of the Judgment to the accused immediately. (MALLANA GOUDA) XXVII Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.
